1.notes:
- **Division A, Title IV general provisions**
  - Sec. 401: appropriations in Act expire at end of current fiscal year unless expressly made longer available.
  - Sec. 402: bars funds for any program/project/activity made known to funded Federal entity/official as noncompliant with Federal law on risk assessment, private property rights protection, or unfunded mandates.
  - Sec. 403: encourages funded departments/agencies, within existing authority/funding, to expand E-Commerce technologies/procedures.
  - Sec. 404: reports/notifications under Act go to House/Senate Appropriations Subcommittees on Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies unless otherwise stated.
  - Sec. 405: bars transfers to U.S. departments/agencies/instrumentalities except under transfer made by/authority in this or another appropriations Act.
  - Sec. 406: bars funds for project/program named for sitting House Member, Delegate, or Resident Commissioner.
  - Sec. 407: agencies receiving funds must post congressional reports on public website if agency head determines national interest; exceptions: national security compromise or confidential/proprietary information; posting only after report available to requesting congressional committees ≥45 days.
  - Sec. 408: bars funds to maintain/establish computer network unless it blocks viewing/downloading/exchanging pornography; exception for law enforcement/criminal investigation, prosecution, adjudication activities.
  - Sec. 409: bars executive-branch agency funds for first-class employee travel contrary to 41 CFR 301-10.122–301-10.124.
  - Sec. 410: bars funds to execute goods/services/construction contracts where contractor has not complied with Executive Order 12989.
  - Sec. 411: bars funds in contravention of 10 U.S.C. 101(e)(8).
  - Sec. 412: bars DOD funds to construct/renovate/expand U.S./territory/possession facility to house Guantanamo detainees for detention/imprisonment in DOD custody/control; exception for modifications at Guantanamo; covered detainees are non-U.S. citizens/non-Armed Forces members located at Guantanamo as of June 24, 2009, in DOD custody/effective control or otherwise detained there.
  - Sec. 413: bars VA use of 38 U.S.C. 5502 to report certain mentally incapacitated/incompetent or extended-loss-of-consciousness persons as adjudicated mental defectives under 18 U.S.C. 922(d)(4)/(g)(4) absent order/finding by competent judicial authority that person is danger to self/others.
  - Citation: division cited as **Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2024**.

- **Division A, title VII general restrictions/authorities (secs. 713–793):**
  - **Sec. 713:** Bars funds in Act for computer networks unless pornography viewing/downloading/exchange is blocked; exception for funds needed by Federal/State/tribal/local law enforcement or entities conducting criminal investigations, prosecution, adjudication.
  - **Sec. 714:** Caps salaries/expenses to carry out section 32 (7 U.S.C. 612c), notwithstanding 7 U.S.C. 612c-6(b), at **$1,574,028,000** excluding prior-year carryover; specified uses: Child Nutrition commodities **$485,000,000**, State Option Contracts **$5,000,000**, defective commodities **$1,660,000**, administration **$37,178,000**. Unobligated balances on Oct. 1, 2024 carry to FY2025 until expended for section 32; clause (3) carryover use capped **$350,000,000** and requires 2-week advance Appropriations notice; bars USDA employee salary/expense use for clause (3), except prior-authorized carryover.
  - **Secs. 715–716, 718–721:** Bars budget language assuming unenacted user fees unless fallback reductions identified; requires 30-day advance written notice/approval for specified reprogrammings/transfers/reorganizations/contracting-out and for changes over **$500,000 or 10%**; requires approval before new prior-year activities; 30-day notice for major capital/IT changes over **$500,000 or 10%**, entities of ≥5 staff, or activities absent from budget request; requires receipt confirmation. Bars disclosure of appropriations hearing materials outside USDA/HHS/CFTC/FCA. Requires prepackaged executive-branch news stories to identify agency preparation/funding unless otherwise authorized. USDA details over **60 days/FY** require full reimbursement. Spending plans due **30 days after enactment**.
  - **Secs. 717, 724–725:** Guaranteed Business and Industry loan one-time fee may be up to **3%** of guaranteed principal notwithstanding 7 U.S.C. 1932(g)(5). Loan/guarantee program levels needing no budget authority may rise up to **25%** with 15-day notice. USDA Working Capital Fund credit-card rebates under 7 U.S.C. 2235a require notice/prior approval; limited to property, plant, equipment and support/IT/cloud systems primarily benefiting USDA agencies.
  - **Food/FDA/nutrition limits:** Sec. 722 bars electronic-only prescribing-professional drug/biologic information absent Federal law. Sec. 726 bars SNAP “variety” rule implementation until 7 CFR 278.1(b)(1)(ii)(C) and 271.2 amended to expand acceptable varieties; interim pre-Agricultural Act of 2014 standards apply. Sec. 737 bars FDA receipt/acknowledgment of IND submissions for heritable human-embryo genetic modification; deemed not received. Sec. 738 bars FDA produce rule enforcement for wine grapes, hops, pulse crops, almonds. Sec. 739 bars enforcement for SY2023-2024 and SY2024-2025 of specified school breakfast vegetable-for-fruit substitution language. Sec. 745 preserves “healthy” claim compliance through FDA final-rule compliance date and preempts nonidentical state requirements during compliance period. Sec. 746 Food for Peace title II aid only with adequate monitoring/controls. Sec. 747 bars China-origin poultry/seafood procurement for child nutrition programs. Sec. 748 paid-lunch equity in SY2024-2025 required only for SFAs with negative balance on June 30, 2023. Secs. 769–770 require reimbursement allowance for low-fat/fat-free flavored milk in specified child nutrition programs and keep SY2023-2024 sodium limits through SY2026-2027; thereafter no more restrictive than 2012 Target 2. Sec. 773 requires 2025 Dietary Guidelines alcohol recommendations to consider NASEM report and follow 7 U.S.C. 5341.

Sec. 727 gives section 502 guaranteed loans/lenders same authority as Housing Act section 538(h),(j). Sec. 728 bars USDA new 31 U.S.C. 9701 user-fee regulations after enactment. Sec. 736 targets at least **10%** of listed rural loan/grant funds to persistent poverty counties; definition includes 20%+ poverty over 30 years or U.S. territories/possessions; program-level application where no budget authority. Sec. 752 allows “Areas Rural in Character” for 2018 broadband pilot eligibility; cap **10%** of relevant Distance Learning/

4.notes:
- **Secs. 534–537 (firearms/arms controls funding limits).**
  - Sec. 534 bars use of funds under this or any Act to require/export-license certain firearm components, parts, accessories, attachments to Canada: Category I, 22 CFR 121.1 (ITAR part 121 as of Apr. 1, 2005), transaction value not over **$500 wholesale**, if exporter meets conditions. Does not waive Shipper’s Export Declaration/notification letter or eligibility to possess/ship/transport/export. License-free export excluded for fully automatic firearms/components except Canadian federal/provincial/municipal end use; barrels, cylinders, receivers/frames, complete breech mechanisms except such government end use; articles for export from Canada onward. Customs district directors/postmasters must permit permanent/temporary export/import specified unclassified articles for Canada/U.S. end use or return. President may temporarily require licenses after Federal Register determination that Canada import controls are inadequate and significant diversion for international terrorism/conflict escalation continues; must terminate when reasons cease.
  - Sec. 535 bars funded denial of applications under **22 U.S.C. 2778(b)(1)(B)**, qualified under **27 CFR 478.112/.113**, to import U.S.-origin “curios or relics” firearms, parts, ammunition.
  - Sec. 536 bars salaries/expenses to deny or fail to act on shotgun import applications if all other legal requirements met and no same-configuration model was denied by Attorney General before Jan. 1, 2011 for lack of sporting suitability/adaptability.
  - Sec. 537 bars use of funds to implement Arms Trade Treaty until Senate approves ratification resolution.

- **Secs. 538–539 (Guantanamo detainees).**
  - Sec. 538 bars funds under this or any Act to transfer, release, or assist transfer/release to/within U.S., territories, possessions Khalid Sheikh Mohammed or any non-U.S.-citizen/non-U.S.-Armed-Forces detainee held on/after June 24, 2009 at Guantanamo by DOD.
  - Sec. 539 bars funds under this or any Act to construct/acquire/modify U.S./territorial/possession facilities to house, for DOD detention/imprisonment, noncitizen/non-military individuals located at Guantanamo as of June 24, 2009 in DOD custody/effective control or otherwise detained there; exception for modifying Guantanamo facilities.

- **Secs. 540–546 (CJS adjustments/law changes).**
  - Sec. 540 rescinds Sept. 30, 2024 unobligated balances from USTR “Salaries and Expenses” and “Trade Enforcement Trust Fund” made by **section 540(a),(b), division B, P.L. 117-328**; reappropriates equal new budget authority Sept. 30, 2024 for FY2024, available to Sept. 30, 2026, same purposes/authorities as **P.L. 116-113**, with “2023” deemed “2026”; emergency designations under **BBEDCA 1985 §251(b)(2)(A)(i)** and referenced FY2022 budget enforcement.
  - Sec. 541 permits Commerce/Justice current and prior unobligated balances, excluding emergency-designated amounts and DOJ “Fees and Expenses of Witnesses,” for payments under **22 U.S.C. 2680b(i)(2)**; caps **$5,000,000 Commerce**, **$10,000,000 Justice**.
  - Sec. 542 makes up to **0.7%** of NTIA IIJA amounts available for salaries/expenses, administration, oversight of NTIA IIJA programs and also Connecting Minority Communities Pilot Program (**P.L. 116-260 div. N §902**) and Broadband Connectivity Infrastructure Program (**§905(d)**), transferable among accounts; no reduction to State allocations under June 30, 2023 notices; 15-day Appropriations notification before obligation; emergency designation retained.
  - Sec. 543 bars funds to move ATF Canine Training Center or ATF National Canine Division from Front Royal, Virginia.
  - Sec. 544 amends **11 U.S.C. 507(d)** by inserting “excluding subparagraph (F)” after “(a)(8)”; effective enactment; not applicable to title 11 cases commenced before enactment.
  - Sec. 545 amends **Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000 §107(b)(2)(C), 22 U.S.C. 7105(b)(2)(C)**, replacing match language with “total project cost” and allowing match generally through approved victim-support contributions/expenditures promoting recovery/reintegration.
  - Sec. 546 directs CHIPS FY2024 allocations within 45 days by Commerce from CHIPS for America Fund under **CHIPS Act §102(a)(1),(2)** and by NSF from Workforce and Education Fund under **§102(d)(1)** per explanatory-statement tables/classified annex; Commerce FY2025 allocation by Oct. 15
